To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) spatial and social structure in host and parasite populations affects the evolution of resistance in hosts and (2) the evolution of host and parasite resistance depends on the relative spatial structure of hosts and parasites.

(i) the spatial structure of host reproduction affects the evolution of resistance in a host population; (ii) the spatial structure affects the evolutionary dynamics of resistance in a way that can be explained in terms of genetic and ecological structuring, and (iii) the spatial structure also affects the coevolution between hosts and parasites, with more mixing leading to higher virulence and reduced resistance.
the spatial structure of a population can strongly influence the evolution of host defence and that this in turn affects the evolution of virulence and transmission in parasites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of host and parasite dispersal in the evolution of resistance to infection.
understanding how spatial structure affects host-parasite coevolution and how this affects the outcome of the coevolution.
the evolution of host-parasite interactions in spatially structured host populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evolution of resistance and the coevolution of host and parasite depends strongly on the spatial and social structure of the population, and that the effects of spatial structuring are not straightforward.
spatial structuring in the host population can lead to the evolution and maintenance of higher levels of resistance than would be expected in a well-mixed population.
the evolution of resistance in spatially structured host populations can be complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of resistance in a spatially structured host population depends on both spatial and social structure.

spatial and social structure can have a profound effect on host resistance and parasite evolution, and that the outcome of coevolution depends critically on the spatial and social structure of the population.
spatial structure in hosts and parasites is a major determinant of the coevolution of resistance and virulence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spatial structure can have profound effects on the evolution of resistance and the outcome of coevolution.
spatial and social structure can strongly affect the evolution of host defence, which in turn can have a large impact on coevolutionary outcomes.
spatial structure can strongly shape the outcome of coevolution.
